titulo: Does turkey make you sleepy on Thanksgiving?
destinatario: se lo manda alguien de la familia al tío que se duerme en el sillón después de la cena y le echa la culpa al pavo
regla_guardable: Sleepy after Thanksgiving? Blame the carbs and the big plate, not the turkey.
fuentes: Christopher Smith, assistant professor of nursing, UNC Charlotte (Nov 2024): turkey has no meaningfully higher tryptophan than chicken, beef, nuts or cheese; main cause is large amounts of carbohydrates; overeating and alcohol also contribute
LiveScience / WHYY / NPR: carbohydrates, overeating and alcohol as the likelier explanations

frases.texto: You blame the turkey for that Thanksgiving nap.
frases.estilo: Dry, direct, with a half smile.

frases.texto: But the turkey isn't the culprit.
A nursing professor at UNC Charlotte says turkey has no meaningfully more tryptophan than chicken, beef, nuts, or cheese.
Tryptophan is the amino acid everyone says makes you drowsy.
He says the main cause is the mountain of carbs: stuffing, mashed potatoes, rolls, and desserts.
Overeating and alcohol pile on too.
Heads up: experts still debate how much each of these matters.
So try a walk after dinner before you blame the bird.
Send this to the uncle who falls asleep on the couch and blames the turkey.
